subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class per-profile browser proxy and per-agent/subagent browser profile binding, and what security model should govern proxy-routed browser sessions?
rationale: The feature changes public config, browser egress routing, logged-in profile/session ownership, and SSRF/credential boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Design the browser-profile contract first
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers define the profile/proxy config shape, SecretRef handling, SSRF gates, subagent inheritance rules, and required upgrade proof.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical issues
options.body: Move broad proxy support, subagent inheritance, and dashboard observability into separate owner-reviewed issues while keeping this as the profile-isolation umbrella.

options.title: Defer to external plugin/workaround
options.body: Close or pause core work and document only current browser.extraArgs/profile workarounds, accepting that per-agent proxy/profile binding remains unsupported.

recommendation.title: Design the browser-profile contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers define the profile/proxy config shape, SecretRef handling, SSRF gates, subagent inheritance rules, and required upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent browser ownership and security-sensitive proxy work make this the best available routing owner for the design decision.
